links.outcome: Factual correctness of MLLM-generated endoscopy findings reports versus human endoscopists
links.effect: Models had superior readability versus humans (p<0.05) but significantly lower factual correctness (p<0.05), driven by over-interpretation and hallucination of visual features.
links.quote: Furthermore, qualitative analysis revealed a "fluency-accuracy paradox": models generated reports with superior linguistic readability compared with humans (p<0.05) but exhibited significantly lower factual correctness (p<0.05) due to "over-interpretation" and hallucination of visual features.

screen.reason: The paper introduces GI-Bench to systematically evaluate multimodal large language models against human endoscopists across gastrointestinal endoscopy clinical tasks, identifying performance bottlenecks and hallucinations without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
